item.title: Senior Chinese, Vietnamese officials hold talks in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
BEIJING, Nov. 3 -- Senior Chinese official He Lifeng held talks with Nguyen Thanh Nghi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) Central Committee and secretary of the CPV Central Committee, in Beijing on Monday. The two sides exchanged views on topics such as economic relations between China and Vietnam, and bilateral economic and trade exchanges and cooperation. He, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China is ready to work with Vietnam to jointly implement the important common understandings reached between the general secretaries of the two parties. He, also director of the Office of the Central Commission for Financial and Economic Affairs, said China is willing to maintain close strategic communication with Vietnam and deepen economic exchanges and mutual learning from each other's experience to advance the building of a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future. Nguyen Thanh Nghi, also chairman of the CPV Central Committee's Commission for Policies and Strategies, said Vietnam is willing to work with China to strengthen the synergy of development strategies and cooperation in economy, trade and other fields, and push for greater progress in the relations between the two parties and the two countries.

item.title: Chinese premier calls for people-centered internet development amid AI advances
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
HANGZHOU, Nov. 3 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Tuesday called for a more people-centered approach to internet development amid rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Li made the remarks in a keynote speech delivered at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, on Tuesday morning. Highlighting that the World Internet Conference has been held for 13 consecutive years, Li stressed that, despite rapid technological advances, one major question of common concern remains unchanged, namely how to make the internet better serve humanity. Li said the internet is undergoing an intelligent transformation and a systemic leap as it increasingly integrates with AI and other technologies. Stressing the need to place greater emphasis on a people-centered approach to internet development in today's world, Li said the ultimate purpose must be to promote the all-round development of people. He emphasized that internet-related technologies should enhance human capabilities, expand choices, affirm human value and improve well-being, rather than make humans subordinate to technology or exacerbate disparities in human development. Calling for joint efforts to build a community with a shared future in cyberspace, Li said China will continue to pursue innovation through openness, promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing, and work with other countries to foster an open, inclusive and dynamic digital innovation ecosystem. On digital security, Li said China will respect the legitimate cybersecurity concerns of all other countries and work together with them to address security challenges, while opposing the creation of a "digital iron curtain." Li also pledged that China will actively implement the Global Development Initiative and support Global South countries in building digital infrastructure and enhancing their digital technology capabilities. About 1,800 participants, including government officials, representatives of international organizations such as the United Nations and global internet companies, as well as experts and scholars, attended the opening ceremony. Following the opening, Li visited the Light of Internet Expo and Wuzhen's World Internet Science and Technology Museum.

item.title: Body of former Chinese vice premier Liu Yandong cremated
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
BEIJING, Nov. 3 -- The body of Liu Yandong, a former Chinese vice premier and state councilor, was cremated in Beijing on Tuesday. She died of illness in Beijing on Oct. 28 at the age of 81. President Xi Jinping and other senior leaders of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the state, including Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng, bid Liu farewell at the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery on Tuesday morning. Amid mournful strains of funeral music, they stood in silent tribute before Liu's remains and paid their final respects with three bows. They shook hands with Liu's family members to offer their condolences. Liu had also served as a member of the Political Bureau of the 17th and 18th CPC Central Committees, and as vice chairperson of the 10th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, China's top political advisory body. She was extolled as an excellent Party member, a time-tested and loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding leader in the CPC's united front work and in the fields of education, science and technology, health, and work for women and children in China. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi, Han Zheng and Hu Jintao, among others, had either visited Liu while she was in the hospital or expressed deep condolences over her passing and offered sincere sympathies to her family members through various means.

item.title: Xi Focus: CPC charts course for tougher action against corruption, stronger self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
BEIJING, Nov. 2 -- As China enters a critical period in its modernization drive, the ruling Communist Party of China (CPC) has charted the course for tougher action against corruption and stronger self-governance in the years ahead. Last week, the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, underscoring the need to step up the fight against corruption and strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power. In doing so, the CPC, the largest political party in the world with more than 100 million members, is seeking to overcome the unique challenges facing a party of its size. These challenges, as outlined by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, include how to maintain the Party's strong governance and leadership capacity, and sustain a clean and upright political environment. "It is now both imperative and timely for the Party to study issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous self-governance," Xi said in a January meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee that set the agenda of the plenum. IMPERATIVE THEME At the January meeting, Xi said the decision to focus the plenary session on Party self-governance had been made after thorough deliberation. Since it was founded in 1921, the Party has attached great importance to its self-supervision and self-governance. Today, the CPC's membership and ranks of officials have undergone structural changes, presenting new challenges for Party building. In response to these challenges, Xi has repeatedly stressed the need for an unwavering commitment to strict Party self-governance, sending a clear signal that discipline will be enforced ever more strictly. "It was with this in mind that the CPC Central Committee decided to make persevering with full and rigorous self-governance the plenum's agenda," he noted. Explaining the resolution at the plenary session, Xi emphasized that persevering with full and rigorous self-governance is essential for maintaining the Party's advanced nature and integrity and consolidating its long-term governing position. This year marks the beginning of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), a critical period for achieving the goal of basically realizing socialist modernization by 2035. "To successfully achieve the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan, it is imperative to focus on enhancing the ability and competence of the Party in leading economic and social development," Xi told senior provincial- and ministerial-level officials attending a study session at the Party School of the CPC Central Committee earlier this year. HOW RESOLUTION TAKES SHAPE In January 2026, a drafting group was set up to prepare the resolution, with Xi at its helm. Throughout the drafting process, he played a decisive role, chairing multiple meetings, delivering important speeches and issuing instructions to guide the work. On Feb. 6, Xi chaired the group's first plenary meeting, where he outlined the key principles for the drafting of the resolution. He called for strict measures to address misconduct and corruption, while stressing that Party building should be pursued as a coordinated whole and integrated with the country's broader development goals. At the same meeting, Xi identified 39 key issues for further study, covering the full scope of Party building and governance. On May 6, Xi chaired a meeting in Shanghai on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, setting out further requirements for the drafting of the resolution. He called for a problem-oriented approach, stressing the need for firm action to tackle prominent problems. As the preparation of the document was underway, Xi stressed the importance of broad consultation and drawing on a wide range of views. He called on non-CPC parties and personages without party affiliation to speak candidly and offer constructive suggestions. During consultation on the draft resolution, 1,173 suggestions for revisions were received from localities, departments and various sectors. After careful consideration, the drafting group incorporated 208 suggestions. The document took shape over more than eight months, with the drafting group holding five plenary meetings and 35 specialized meetings. During the plenary session last week, participants held in-depth discussions and exchanged views, putting forward suggestions that led to 13 revisions to the draft resolution before it was finally adopted on Oct. 29. WHY RESOLUTION MATTERS The resolution examines new circumstances, challenges and tasks facing the Party as it advances full and rigorous Party self-governance. It identifies three increasingly arduous tasks for the CPC: safeguarding China's sovereignty, security and development interests amid a changing international environment; advancing reform and development while maintaining social harmony and stability at home; and preserving the Party's advanced nature and integrity. It also warns that, under new circumstances marked by profound changes, the Party faces challenges to its governance and leadership capacity, the quality of its membership, and its resistance against corruption and moral decline. The resolution has established a problem-oriented approach as one of the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. It places particular emphasis on strengthening Party spirit among CPC members, as problems in Party conduct and discipline often stem from a lack of strong Party spirit. The resolution sets out specific measures to ensure that Party members and officials remain loyal, upright, and responsible. Another focus is eliminating hidden rules and curbing malpractices such as cultivating connections and making back-room deals. The resolution sets out concrete measures to root out such practices. The more than 200 measures outlined in the resolution combine the reinforcement of existing requirements with new responses to emerging challenges. In the fight against corruption, for example, the resolution calls for intensified efforts to expose new and concealed forms of graft. These include the use of proxies, or so-called "white gloves," to disguise illicit dealings, as well as the "revolving door" phenomenon of bureaucrat-merchant collusion after officials' retirement. It also calls for a crackdown on corruption involving the internet, virtual currencies, cross-border capital flows and blockchain technology. The resolution also sets out measures to improve the Party and state oversight systems and ensure that political responsibility for full and rigorous Party self-governance is effectively discharged. "No other political party in the world takes its own development as seriously as the CPC does, or advances its own self-reform with such a high degree of self-awareness, scientific rigor and systematic effort," Xi has said. "This is a distinctive strength of our Party." The resolution, as observers point out, signals a renewed commitment by the CPC to advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, recognizing this as a fundamental underpinning of the broader endeavor to build China into a strong country and advance national rejuvenation. "We have already forged a bright path ahead, and we must keep moving forward," Xi has said.

item.title: Chinese vice premier urges strengthening advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
NANJING, Nov. 2 -- Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing has stressed the need to vigorously develop advanced manufacturing and nurture small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that use specialized and sophisticated technologies to produce novel and unique products. Zhang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during his inspection tour in the eastern province of Jiangsu from Sunday to Monday. During the inspection tour, Zhang emphasized the need to accelerate the building of a modern industrial system and continuously cultivate new growth drivers and strengths for development. In Nanjing and Huai'an, Zhang visited enterprises in such sectors as smart grid and new materials. He stressed the need to vigorously develop next-generation intelligent manufacturing and to provide guidance and support for more enterprises in their digital and intelligent transformation. Efforts should be made to upgrade technologies and processes in traditional industries and optimize their product mix, accelerate the large-scale application of emerging industries, and strengthen forward-looking planning for future industries, said Zhang. Zhang stressed the need to support these specialized and sophisticated SMEs in increasing research and development investment and striving for new breakthroughs in original innovation and in key core and cutting-edge technologies. He also called for encouraging large enterprises to open up application scenarios and share factor resources, to help more specialized and sophisticated SMEs integrate into their supply chains, innovation chains and value chains.

item.title: Xi stresses improving protection, coordination to make Yellow River more beautiful
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 2 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has stressed efforts to continuously improve protection and coordination to make the Yellow River more beautiful. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on further advancing the protection and governance of the Yellow River. Xi emphasized that solid efforts must be made to promote ecological protection and high-quality development in the Yellow River Basin, carry forward the Yellow River culture, and ensure that this mother river delivers sustainable benefits to the Chinese nation and future generations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a work conference on comprehensively advancing the protection and governance of the Yellow River, held on Monday in Zhengzhou, central China's Henan Province. Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the conference. He called for joint efforts to advance greater protection and coordinated governance of the Yellow River, ensure the river is well managed, and enhance the conservation and intensive utilization of water resources. The conference briefed participants on the achievements in Yellow River governance over the past 80 years under the leadership of the CPC. Thanks to 80 years of conservation efforts, the river, once prone to devastating floods, heavy sedimentation and shifting channels, now has cleaner waters and more sustainable water use. The Yellow River, China's second-longest river, flows 5,464 km through nine provinces and autonomous regions, crossing deserts and loess lands, before emptying into the Bohai Sea in Shandong.

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 2 -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon.

item.title: China issues regulation on registration, management of public institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
BEIJING, Oct. 26 -- China has issued a regulation on the registration and management of public institutions, aiming to strengthen the Party's overall leadership over such institutions and reinforce their commitment to serving the public interest. Premier Li Qiang signed a State Council decree promulgating the regulation, which consists of six chapters and 34 articles and will take effect on Dec. 1. The regulation also standardizes registration and management procedures and safeguards public institutions' legitimate rights and interests. It requires public institutions to uphold the leadership of the Communist Party of China, firmly implement the Party's lines, principles and policies, and step up efforts to improve conduct, enforce discipline and combat corruption. It also calls on public institutions to remain committed to serving the public interest, prioritize social benefits, and continuously improve the quality and efficiency of their public services. The regulation further stipulates that competent authorities and sponsoring organizations must oversee and guide public institutions to ensure their activities are conducted in accordance with the law. Industry regulators, including those in the medical, educational and scientific research sectors, are also required to strengthen supervision and inspections of relevant institutions' conduct. To improve registration services, the regulation calls for standardized and streamlined procedures. Registration authorities and public institutions are required to promptly disclose relevant information through the national public institution registration and management information platform, in accordance with the law.
